question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's position as General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and Chairman of the Central Military Commission remains firmly entrenched through late 2026, with no scheduled leadership transition or visible factional challenges ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in 2027. Recent personnel decisions, ongoing anti-corruption efforts within the PLA, and policy continuity reflect his appointment of most current elites and the absence of identifiable pathways for abrupt removal outside established party mechanisms. Trader consensus at 95.5% for continued leadership aligns with historical patterns where major shifts occur at congresses rather than through sudden ousters. Low-probability developments that could still shift odds include a sudden health event, severe economic crisis prompting elite realignment, or unforeseen external shock before year-end.

eventMetadata.context_description: Democratic voters and traders remain divided heading into the 2028 nomination cycle, with no candidate yet securing dominant support in an open field. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s early polling edge in New Hampshire and her comments that she has not ruled out a bid have boosted her position among progressives, while Gavin Newsom leverages his California governorship for visibility and Jon Ossoff draws attention as a Georgia senator with crossover appeal. The Democratic National Committee’s newly approved 2028 primary calendar, which elevates South Carolina, Nevada, and other states with strong Black, Latino, and union voters ahead of Iowa, introduces new strategic dynamics that could reward candidates who perform well in those early contests. Midterm results, fundraising hauls, and endorsements from party figures will likely influence trader assessments as the race fragments among moderates and progressives.
